observations: LM2 Torah 75 is a two-paragraph aphoristic teaching with no bechina (parallel-nature) language. The entire argument is eitza (causal): the Rebbe establishes that the tzaddik is greater than Torah itself (citing the Talmud, Makkot 22b, that people rise for a great person but not for a Torah scroll), then applies a kal va-chomer: if Torah's inner light (המאור שבה) returns one to the right path, then certainly the light of the tzaddik — even merely gazing at him — helps greatly for holiness. The relationship between הסתכלות בצדיק and קדושה is directional and causal (gazing produces holiness), not a shared-essence bechina. Since no group of 3 or more concepts is connected by explicit bechina language in this text, and since the text does not establish any independent thematic domain through parallel equating, no new packages can be proposed. The teaching's content is best understood as a single eitza statement within a larger cross-Torah package for the tzaddik-holiness domain.
